Class WifiProvisioner

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.api.net.WifiProvisioner
public final class WifiProvisioner extends Object
Wi-Fi provisioning without baking credentials into the firmware, written in plain Java on top of Wifi and HttpServer (it adds no intrinsics, and costs nothing in a program that does not call it). run(String, String) opens an access point, serves an HTML form on port 80 and joins the network the user submits. The caller must have started Serial first.

On UNO R4 WiFi the whole flow runs on the board: join the access point, open http://192.168.4.1/, enter the SSID and password, and the board drops the access point, joins that network and prints its address over Serial. If the connection fails within 15000 ms the access point comes back so the form can be submitted again. The credentials live only in RAM.

On UNO Q Wi-Fi belongs to Linux, which the MCU cannot reconfigure: start the hotspot there first (nmcli device wifi hotspot ssid <ssid> password <password>). The form is then served through arduino-router, and the submitted credentials are printed over Serial for Linux to apply (nmcli device wifi connect <ssid> password <password>).

Limits: SSID and password are at most 31 characters each (Juno's runtime strings are small), and the form is plain HTTP, so the password crosses the setup network unencrypted; on UNO R4 WiFi the access point's own WPA2 passphrase is what protects it.

    • run

      public static void run(String apSsid, String apPassword)
      Serves the setup form until credentials are submitted and, on UNO R4 WiFi, the board has joined that network; on UNO Q it returns once the credentials have been printed. apPassword is a WPA2 passphrase of at least 8 characters, or empty for an open access point.
